miriam: Quick flag — new candidate ranky-3b-ptq (post-PTQ) looks fine on overall NDCG but we're seeing a reproducible MRR drop on long queries compared to fp16. Can someone take a quick look? :thinking:

sam: Thanks, can you paste the evaluation command you used? also which dataset slice counts as 'long'? :eyes:

miriam: Ran on `golden-anchors-v2` + full holdout. Long = queries with token_count >= 128. Command was:
```
./eval/run_eval.sh --model ranky-3b-ptq --baseline ranky-3b-fp16 --cohort golden-anchors-v2 --slices "len>=128,len<128" --metrics ndcg@10,mrr@10 --seed 42
```

eval-bot: Quick summary (from that run):
- overall ndcg@10: ptq 0.712 vs fp16 0.715 (delta -0.003)
- long queries mrr@10: ptq 0.396 vs fp16 0.432 (delta -0.036) :large_red_circle:
- short queries mrr@10: ptq 0.512 vs fp16 0.508 (delta +0.004)
p-values (bootstrap): overall ndcg p=0.18, long mrr p=0.0014

jon: Oof, top-of-list degradation for long queries only. First checks: tokenization parity (vocab/merge ops), context truncation, and candidate ordering before rerank. PTQ sometimes shifts subtle logits so tie-breaking changes.

dinesh: Agree — also check the candidate pool composition: did the upstream retriever change? If topk distribution shifted, reranker sees different tails. Could be apparent quality drop even if reranker unchanged.

miriam: Good call. I pinned retriever commit used in eval: `retriever@cb9f3c` (same as baseline). Tokenizer: baseline used `tokenizer:v1.4`, PTQ run used the same docker image but maybe different tokenizer binary.

sam: I'll run a tokenizer parity diff + rerun with exact candidate ids. Quick script: 
```
python tools/check_token_parity.py --model ranky-3b-ptq --baseline ranky-3b-fp16 --cohort golden-anchors-v2 --slice len>=128 
```
I'll also dump top5 candidate ids for first 200 long queries.

eval-bot: parity script output (sanity): 98.9% tokenization match, 2.1% of long queries have a subtle whitespace normalization diff.

jon: That 2% could be concentrated in tail docs that affect top1. Also run a run with `--preserve-candidate-order` to rule out ranking jitter due to tie-handling.

dinesh: For significance: recommend bootstrap CI on MRR difference for the long-slice with 10k resamples and report 95% CI. If CI excludes 0, this is real. Also do stratified bootstrap by query length bucket (128-256, 256+).

miriam: I'll queue those. If this is real and concentrated in 256+ queries, we should either hold the PTQ rollout for rerank or patch quantization parameters (per-layer clipping).

sam: Ran preserve-order + exact-tokenizer run and posted artifacts to s3://redwood-evals/ranky3b/5076543210. Quick diff: MRR long (preserve-order) ptq 0.402 vs fp16 0.431 (delta -0.029). Still down but smaller.

eval-bot: Bootstrap 95% CI for long MRR delta (ptq - fp16): [-0.042, -0.018] (10k resamples) — excludes 0.

miriam: Thank you all. Action items: (1) rollback PTQ candidate from the canary queue for rerank until we isolate cause, (2) jon/dinesh to try per-layer clip tuning and re-eval on 128-256 vs 256+, (3) sam to produce a short report with top affected queries (s3 link) and tokenization diffs. I'll open an ops ticket for the rollback. :white_check_mark:

jon: I'll try per-layer clip tweaks and run targeted evals by EOD. If we can recover top1 for 256+ with modest clip changes, we can reattempt PTQ.

dinesh: Also adding a quick trace to check kv-cache behaviour for long contexts — maybe pad-handling changed in PTQ runtime.

miriam: Cool. If anyone finds a smoking gun ping me. Thanks for quick triage. :raised_hands:
